description_full: VEON Ltd. provides telecommunications and digital services in Pakistan, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Bangladesh, and Uzbekistan. The company offers mobile telecommunications services under prepaid and postpaid subscriptions, including value-added and call completion services, national and international roaming services, wireless Internet access, mobile financial services, and mobile bundles; fixed-line telecommunications using fiber optic networks; cross-border transmission services; prepaid scratch cards and electronic recharge options; mobile services on 2G, 3G, and 4G/LTE networks; cloud solutions, including consumer storage apps; local, long-distance, and international voice services; and customer support through contact centers. It also provides FikrFree, a digital insurance marketplace; Tamasha, a video streaming app; ROX, a digital lifestyle brand; Garaj, a cloud platform; ApnaClinic and Helsi digital healthcare platforms; SIMOSA, ZARR, and RYZE lifestyle platforms; Kyivstar TV, a media streaming service; My Kyivstar, a self-service application; Uklon, a ride-hailing and delivery platform; Adwisor, an adtech platform; Simply, a mobile-only neobank; BeeTV, an entertainment platform; Hitter and riitm music streaming platforms; MyBL, Janymda, and Hambi super-apps; AI tutor, an AI-powered learning assistant; Toffee, an infotainment platform; BCloud, a digital infrastructure solution; Beepul, a financial services solution; KINOM, a digital entertainment platform; BeeMarket, an electronics and home appliance marketplace; Hambi Davo, a suite of digital health services; and OQ, a digital platform. The company distributes its products and services through a direct sales force, franchises, third-party retailers, distributors, supermarkets, stores, chains, online, offices, and other channels. The company was formerly known as VimpelCom Ltd. and changed its name to VEON Ltd. in March 2017. VEON Ltd. was founded in 1992 and is headquartered in Dubai, the United Arab Emirates.
ceo_bio: Mr. Muhterem Kaan Terzioglu | Group CEO & Director | Age 57 | Compensation: $3.8M (FY2024)
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 18K people. Revenue per employee of $232K ranks in the bottom quartile among Communication Services peers, declining at 9%/yr — weakening productivity. Each employee generates $35K of free cash flow annually. CEO compensation is 17× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity).
financial_summary: VEON Ltd. is a mid-cap communication services business with a $5.3B market cap on $4.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +5% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 21% against a 10% cost of capital — a 11-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.
The business throws off $665M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.7× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 2.7× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield of 3.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 2.2% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 33% operating margin runs 24pp above the Communication Services median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.59x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.3% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+2.2% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.06 across 169 companies in the universe; the top four hold 36% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 71% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 13% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 46% and a beta of 1.09, it moves roughly with the market.
About $11.1M trades a day, enough to build a position, and interest is running hot at 1.7x its yearly average volume.
In past sell-offs it fell 52% in the 2020 crash, 85% in the 2022 bear market and 89% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 58% below its blended-model fair value of $187, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 25%), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Communication Services peers: cheaper on EV/EBITDA 4.7 vs 9.4 and P/FCF 8.0 vs 11.3, richer on P/E 98.2 vs 14.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 45% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 12.4% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 16.4% (vs the 8% bar).
The 8 covering analysts target $90.02 on average, 16% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 21% clears the cost of capital of 10.3% by 11pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.63).
It converts 15% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality is a concern: a weak Piotroski score of 3/9.
ROE of 44% is amplified by 6.9x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.
Operating margin is running 12pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.7x net debt to EBITDA ($1.7B of cash against $3.1B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.7x.
Warning signs: an Altman Z of 0.95 in the distress zone, which caps the rating at HOLD.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 5.4% over 3 years and -11.2% over 5 years, so growth is accelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 18%).
At current returns, reinvesting 32% of profits supports about 6.8% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.2%, and institutions hold 23%.
Insiders have only bought over the past year (3 purchases, net $1.1M bought).
It returns 3.2% a year to shareholders (2.0% in buybacks).
The share count has grown 1.0% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 18,938 employees, each generates about $232K of revenue, 0.4x the Communication Services median, and productivity has fallen 9.1% a year.
That works out to $35K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.8M (17x revenue per employee).
